Attention and Memory in Small Models

Ada LovelaceAnalytical Engines Ltd , Alan Turing
Abstract

We study how attention and memory trade off in models below ten million parameters. A key-value memory of size m recovers most of the accuracy lost when attention heads are pruned, and the effect holds across three tasks.

1 Introduction

Small language models are deployed where memory and latency are scarce. Prior work [1, 2] shows attention is the dominant cost at long context, while retrieval-augmented models [3] move knowledge into an external store.

2 Method

We replace h of the H attention heads with a memory read whose cost is O per token.

2.1 Training

All models are trained for 20k steps with AdamW and a batch of 256 sequences.

3 Results

With half the heads removed, memory recovers 7.1 of the 8.2 points lost.
